items.problem: Bootstrap omitted UWP project items linked from outside the Source directory.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 121-148 reports only 4 copied files and zero TODOs; source MobileHotspot.csproj lines 94-165 links shared App/MainPage/Styles/scenario XAML/assets; build lines 3564-3608 show missing scenario types and XAML compiler failures.
items.skill_search: Searched Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 for Link, Include, shared, and external; copy logic only recursively enumerated $Source.
items.root_cause: The bootstrap treated physical directory membership as the complete project inventory rather than honoring evaluated Include/Link metadata.
items.proposed_fix: Teach Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 to resolve common project properties and copy linked supported files to their Link target paths before rewrite/triage.
items.generalizes: UWP SDK samples and shared-code solutions routinely link XAML, code-behind, resources, and assets from sibling SharedContent directories.

items.problem: Defensive UI guidance explicitly told the agent to replace the primary feature surface when hardware was unavailable.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 4161-4164 implements ShowUnavailable by collapsing HotspotPanel; migration-score.json records both features fail because all named controls are absent.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md section 'Defensive UI for device-dependent features', former line 200.
items.wrong_text_if_any: on catch, swap the page's main content for the fallback
items.root_cause: The fallback rule optimized for non-blank screenshots but contradicted the higher-priority fidelity rule and removed the UI surface under test.
items.proposed_fix: Require original named controls to remain visible and identifiable, disable device-dependent actions, and add an adjacent status message.
items.generalizes: Camera, microphone, location, sensor, Bluetooth, NFC, networking, and other hardware-dependent migrations are frequently validated on machines without the device.

items.problem: The skill prescribed a nonexistent winapp build command and the launch helper ignored default dotnet output layout.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 3340-3403 shows winapp build rejected; lines 3892-3900 shows Test-AppLaunch unavailable because it searched only bin\x64\Debug after a successful default dotnet build.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md Step 3/final build and Test-AppLaunch.ps1 binCandidates.
items.root_cause: Command and output-layout assumptions no longer matched the installed CLI and native dotnet workflow.
items.proposed_fix: Use dotnet build in the workflow and search both Platform-qualified and default bin\Debug layouts.
items.generalizes: Every migrated project uses the same current WinUI scaffold and build/launch workflow.

items.problem: Project reconciliation did not explicitly preserve or derive the minimum Windows version required by retained APIs.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 3861-3869 and 4130-4153 show repeated CA1416 warnings until TargetPlatformMinVersion and manifest MinVersion moved from 17763 to 19041.
items.skill_search: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #csproj mentioned current TFMs but did not instruct how to reconcile TargetPlatformMinVersion or CA1416.
items.root_cause: The scaffold minimum was retained even though migrated API contracts required a newer minimum.
items.proposed_fix: Document that source/API requirements govern TargetPlatformMinVersion and manifest MinVersion, with CA1416 as the check signal.
items.generalizes: Many UWP APIs were introduced after the WinUI scaffold's broad default minimum and emit CA1416 when migrated unchanged.
